[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Agent-executable task specs (PTN-APP-GOV-005) require acceptance criteria that are independently verifiable. When these criteria are written as prose — "the endpoint handles timezone conversion correctly" — the agent interprets "correctly" based on its training data, producing output that may or may not match the product owner's intent. The spec author attempts to close this gap by writing more detailed prose, but detailed prose introduces its own ambiguity: "handles DST boundaries" means different things to different engineers and different model runs. The fundamental problem is that prose acceptance criteria are not executable — they cannot be automatically verified.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

The BDD Scenario as Agent Acceptance Criteria Pattern replaces prose acceptance criteria with references to `@FR-` tagged Gherkin scenario IDs from committed `.feature` files. Each acceptance criterion checkbox maps to a specific scenario in a `.feature` file that already exists in the repository. The agent's success is defined by scenario passage — deterministic, automated, and unambiguous. The `.feature` file is assembled into the agent's context window alongside the spec, giving the agent both the success criteria (scenario IDs) and the behavioral specification (Given/When/Then steps) it must satisfy.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- When an agent-executable task spec targets a concern that has committed `.feature` files in `docs/requirements/functional/`
- When the agent's output is production code or step definitions that must pass BDD scenarios
- When the definition of "done" for an agent task is scenario passage, not prose interpretation
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#target-audience]

### Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Engineers** authoring agent-executable task specs for BDD-driven implementation work
- **Platform Engineers** configuring the context assembly stage of the agent dispatch pipeline
- **Engineering Leads** establishing conventions for how BDD scenarios are referenced in agent specs
page_texts.8:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **Deterministic acceptance**: The agent either makes the scenario pass or it doesn't — there is no subjective interpretation of "done"
- **Pre-existing specification**: The `.feature` file is committed before the agent runs — the product owner has already approved the behavioral intent
- **Automated verification**: The BDD runner is the acceptance gate — the reviewing engineer checks that scenarios pass, not that prose criteria are subjectively met
- **Per-language decomposition**: Combined with the per-language issue decomposition from the BDD lifecycle strategy, each spec targets a single language and a bounded set of scenarios

page_texts.10:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The [BDD-Driven SDLC Strategy](../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/bdd-lifecycle-strategy.md) establishes that `.feature` files are the authoritative requirement specification. The [Machine-Readable Agent Specification Pattern](./PTN-APP-GOV-005-machine-readable-agent-specification-pattern.md) defines the structured template agents receive as input. This pattern bridges the two: it defines how the content of the `.feature` file populates the Acceptance Criteria section of the agent spec.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The agent dispatch pipeline (PTN-TEC-AI-002) assembles a context window from the spec body and injected enterprise context. When acceptance criteria reference `@FR-` scenario IDs, the pipeline can resolve those IDs to specific scenarios in committed `.feature` files and include the full Gherkin text in the context window. This gives the agent:

1. The **scenario ID** — what must pass (the checkbox)
2. The **Given/When/Then steps** — the behavioral specification (the implementation target)
3. The **`.feature` file path** — the file the agent's step definitions must reference
page_texts.12:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Prose acceptance criteria in agent specs produce three failure modes that BDD scenario references eliminate:

- **Ambiguous success definition**: "Rate limiting works correctly" is not falsifiable. `@FR-CLK-TZ-010 — now_local converts to user timezone` is falsifiable — the scenario either passes or fails.
- **Missing edge cases**: Prose criteria tend to describe the happy path. A `.feature` file with 5 scenarios covers the happy path, error cases, and boundary conditions — the agent implements against all of them, not just the obvious case.
- **Verification labor**: A reviewer reading prose criteria must manually judge whether the agent's output satisfies each criterion. A reviewer checking `@FR-` scenario passage looks at the CI report — each scenario is green or red.
page_texts.13:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- The `.feature` file must be committed to the repository before the agent spec is triggered — the BDD lifecycle requires spec-before-code
- The agent spec must follow PTN-APP-GOV-005 structure — this pattern extends that template, not replaces it
- Per-language decomposition (one issue per `.feature` file per language) keeps the scope bounded — the agent does not implement across all languages in one spec
- The pipeline's context assembly stage must resolve `@FR-` IDs to Gherkin content — this requires read access to the canonical `.feature` file path

page_texts.15:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

The BDD Scenario as Agent Acceptance Criteria Pattern defines a convention for writing the Acceptance Criteria section of an agent-executable task spec when the task is BDD-driven implementation work:

1. **Each checkbox references an `@FR-` scenario ID** and a brief description from the scenario name
2. **At least one additional checkbox** references a technical verification (e.g., "all existing tests pass")
3. **The Constraints section** references the canonical `.feature` file path
4. **The pipeline** resolves the `@FR-` IDs and injects the full Gherkin content into the agent's context
page_texts.16:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#spec-structure]

### Spec Structure

```markdown
## Goal
Implement the Clock timezone conversion concern in Python. All scenarios in
`docs/requirements/functional/clock/timezone.feature` must pass using pytest-bdd.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] @FR-CLK-TZ-010 — now_local converts to user timezone
- [ ] @FR-CLK-TZ-020 — to_local handles DST boundary correctly
- [ ] @FR-CLK-TZ-030 — now_local rejects unknown timezone identifier
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass (`task python:test` exits 0)

## Constraints
- Follow: Project Gherkin conventions (docs/requirements/functional/README.md)
- Follow: Python standards (eap-ref-architecture/standards/technology/python/)
- Source: docs/requirements/functional/clock/timezone.feature
- Target: components/python/src/ for implementation, components/python/tests/clock/ for step defs
- Only modify files in components/python/ — do not modify other language components
- Do not modify the .feature file — it is the requirement, not an implementation artifact

## Enterprise Work Item
WI#1234
```

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```
Spec Authoring                    Pipeline Context Assembly
──────────────                    ─────────────────────────

Engineer writes spec              Pipeline resolves @FR- IDs
with @FR- scenario IDs            from committed .feature file
        │                                  │
        ▼                                  ▼
┌──────────────────┐            ┌──────────────────────────┐
│ ## Acceptance     │            │ Agent Context Window     │
│ Criteria          │            │                          │
│                   │            │ [Spec Body]              │
│ - [ ] @FR-CLK-   │────────────│ Goal: Implement Clock... │
│       TZ-010     │            │ AC: @FR-CLK-TZ-010...    │
│ - [ ] @FR-CLK-   │            │                          │
│       TZ-020     │            │ [Resolved .feature]      │
│ - [ ] @FR-CLK-   │            │ Feature: Clock Timezone  │
│       TZ-030     │            │   Scenario: now_local... │
│                   │            │     Given a UTC time...  │
└──────────────────┘            │     When now_local is... │
                                │     Then the result...   │
                                └──────────────────────────┘
                                           │
                                           ▼
                                ┌──────────────────────────┐
                                │ Agent Implementation     │
                                │                          │
                                │ Writes:                  │
                                │  - Step definitions      │
                                │  - Production code       │
                                │                          │
                                │ Verifies:                │
                                │  - BDD runner passes     │
                                │    all @FR- scenarios    │
                                └──────────────────────────┘
```
page_texts.18:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#rules]

### Rules

1. **Every `@FR-` scenario in the referenced `.feature` file must appear as a checkbox.** Partial coverage is not permitted — the agent implements all scenarios in the file, not a subset.

2. **At least one non-scenario criterion must be present.** Typically "all existing tests continue to pass" — this prevents the agent from breaking adjacent functionality while satisfying the new scenarios.

3. **The `.feature` file must be committed before the spec is triggered.** The pipeline resolves `@FR-` IDs from committed content. An `@FR-` reference to an uncommitted scenario is a validation failure.

4. **One spec per `.feature` file per language.** The per-language decomposition from the BDD lifecycle strategy ensures bounded scope. A spec that targets "all languages" violates PTN-APP-GOV-005's bounded scope principle and the file count heuristic in [GUID-GOV-IMPL-003](../../../strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-003-ai-agent-spec-authoring-guidance.md).

5. **The Constraints section must include the `.feature` file path.** This enables the pipeline to resolve the file and inject its content. Use the canonical path (`docs/requirements/functional/...`), not a language copy path.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#step-1--commit-the-feature-file-first]

### Step 1 — Commit the `.feature` File First

Before writing the agent spec, ensure the `.feature` file exists in `docs/requirements/functional/<concern>/` and has been synced to language test directories per [PTN-APP-TEST-001](../testing/PTN-APP-TEST-001-polyglot-feature-file-sync-pattern.md). The scenarios in the file are the requirements the agent will implement against.
page_texts.21:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#step-2--write-the-spec-using-fr--references]

### Step 2 — Write the Spec Using `@FR-` References

Open a new issue using the agent task template (PTN-APP-GOV-005). In the Acceptance Criteria section, list each `@FR-` scenario ID from the `.feature` file as a checkbox:

```markdown
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] @FR-CLK-TZ-010 — now_local converts to user timezone
- [ ] @FR-CLK-TZ-020 — to_local handles DST boundary correctly
- [ ] @FR-CLK-TZ-030 — now_local rejects unknown timezone identifier
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass
```

The description after the `@FR-` ID is the scenario name from the `.feature` file. It aids human readability during review.
page_texts.22:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#step-3--scope-to-a-single-language]

### Step 3 — Scope to a Single Language

Create one spec per language. The Goal names the specific language and its BDD runner:

| Language | Goal Pattern |
|----------|-------------|
| Python | "...must pass using pytest-bdd" |
| C# | "...must pass using SpecFlow/Reqnroll" |
| Java | "...must pass using Cucumber-JVM" |
| Rust | "...must pass using cucumber-rs" |

The Constraints section uses language-specific paths:

| Language | Target Constraint |
|----------|------------------|
| Python | `components/python/src/` and `components/python/tests/<concern>/` |
| C# | `components/dotnet/src/` and `components/dotnet/tests/Mmes.Common.Core.Tests/<Concern>/` |
| Java | `components/java/src/` and `components/java/src/test/java/.../steps/` |
| Rust | `components/rust/src/` and `components/rust/tests/steps/` |
page_texts.23:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#step-4--configure-pipeline-context-assembly]

### Step 4 — Configure Pipeline Context Assembly

The agent dispatch pipeline's context assembly stage (PTN-APP-GOV-002) must resolve `.feature` file content when the spec contains `@FR-` references. The assembly logic:

1. Parse the Constraints section for a line matching `Source: docs/requirements/functional/...`
2. Read the referenced `.feature` file from the repository
3. Inject the full Gherkin content into the agent's context window, after the spec body
4. The agent receives both "what must pass" (the `@FR-` checkboxes) and "what the behavior is" (the Given/When/Then steps)
page_texts.24:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#step-5--apply-the-sod-control]

### Step 5 — Apply the SOD Control

Per the BDD lifecycle strategy and [GUID-GOV-IMPL-003](../../../strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-003-ai-agent-spec-authoring-guidance.md):

1. The engineer writes the spec and applies the routing label (`agent:implementation`)
2. A peer reviewer validates the spec — confirming `@FR-` IDs match the committed `.feature` file and the scope is bounded to one language
3. The peer reviewer applies `agent-task` to trigger the pipeline

The author never self-triggers.

---
page_texts.26:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#traceability-chain]

### Traceability Chain

BDD scenario references in agent specs create an unbroken traceability chain:

```
ADO Work Item (WI#1234)
  └── GitHub Issue #88 (references WI#1234)
       ├── Acceptance Criteria: @FR-CLK-TZ-010, @FR-CLK-TZ-020, @FR-CLK-TZ-030
       └── PR #92 (linked to Issue #88)
            └── BDD runner report: @FR-CLK-TZ-010 PASS, @FR-CLK-TZ-020 PASS, @FR-CLK-TZ-030 PASS
```

The `@FR-` IDs are the shared identifiers that connect the requirement (`.feature` file), the task spec (GitHub Issue), the implementation (PR), and the verification (CI report). No separate traceability exercise is needed — the chain is a byproduct of using `@FR-` references.
page_texts.27:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#scenario-integrity]

### Scenario Integrity

The peer reviewer (Step 5) must verify that the `@FR-` IDs in the spec match the scenarios in the committed `.feature` file. This prevents:

- Referencing scenarios that don't exist (typo in the `@FR-` ID)
- Omitting scenarios (cherry-picking easy scenarios, skipping edge cases)
- Referencing scenarios from a different `.feature` file than the one named in Constraints
page_texts.28:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#phipii-compliance]

### PHI/PII Compliance

`.feature` files referenced by agent specs must not contain PHI/PII — this is enforced by the BDD lifecycle strategy and the pipeline's content screening (GUID-SEC-AI-AGENTPIPE-2.9.08). Because the `.feature` file content is injected into the agent's context window, any sensitive data in the file would flow into the agent's processing context.

page_texts.32:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#example-3--anti-pattern-do-not-use]

### Example 3 — Anti-Pattern (Do Not Use)

```markdown
## Goal
Implement timezone handling across all languages.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Timezone conversion works correctly
- [ ] Tests pass

## Constraints
- Follow coding standards

## Enterprise Work Item
WI#1234
```

> This spec violates four rules: the Goal spans all languages (unbounded), the AC are prose ("works correctly" is not falsifiable), there are no `@FR-` references, and the Constraints name no specific files or standards.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-006-bdd-scenario-agent-acceptance-criteria-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem**: Prose acceptance criteria in agent specs are ambiguous — different model runs interpret "works correctly" differently, producing non-deterministic output.

**Solution**: Replace prose AC with `@FR-` tagged Gherkin scenario ID references from committed `.feature` files. The agent's success is scenario passage — deterministic, automated, and unambiguous. The pipeline injects the full Gherkin content into the agent's context window.

**Key Rules**: Every `@FR-` scenario in the `.feature` file gets a checkbox. One spec per `.feature` file per language. The `.feature` file must be committed before the spec is triggered. The author never self-triggers — a peer reviewer applies `agent-task`.

**Where it fits**: Specializes PTN-APP-GOV-005 (spec template) for BDD-driven work. Depends on PTN-APP-TEST-001 (feature file sync) for file management. Implements Phase 3 of the BDD-Driven SDLC Strategy.
